title: Capability-scope fail-closed rework denies internal approval-inbox/durable-tasks MCP servers in any scoped workspace (approval-path DoS)
claim: The security fix (29ebf44a8) that closed XC-authz-injection-chains-6 removed the internal-server exemption in the executeMcpRuntime choke point. executeMcpRuntime now calls enforceMcpServerScope(input) UNCONDITIONALLY (tool-invocation-coordinator-service.ts:927) before dispatching to the internal approval-inbox (:931) or durable-tasks (:938) handlers. enforceMcpServerScope → host.assertMcpServerInScope → assertMcpServerInCapabilityScope (gateway-service.ts:7942) → isCapabilityAllowed(effective, request.serverId). The internal server IDs (goatcitadel-internal-approval-inbox, goatcitadel-internal-durable-tasks) are never seeded into capability_scope_assignments, and computeEffectiveSet (capability-scope-resolver.ts:31) returns an allowlist built solely from the workspace/citadel assignment rows whenever ANY mcp_server row exists. So in a capability-scoped workspace the internal IDs are absent from the effective set and isCapabilityAllowed returns false → PolicyViolationError → the approval-inbox and durable-tasks MCP tools are blocked. This breaks operators/agents responding to approvals and managing durable tasks via those internal surfaces — a safety/governance path — in exactly the workspaces capability scoping is built for. Additionally, the resolver fault fallback was flipped from ALL_CAPABILITIES to NO_CAPABILITIES (capability-scope-resolver.ts:93), so any transient resolver fault now denies ALL MCP including internal (previously fail-open, comment said 'never narrow a turn due to a fault').
evidence: tool-invocation-coordinator-service.ts:923-930 (comment explicitly states the gate now 'applies to internal MCP surfaces too, including durable tasks' and enforceMcpServerScope runs before the isInternalMcpApprovalInboxServer/isInternalMcpDurableTasksServer dispatch at :931/:938). gateway-service.ts:1413 wires assertMcpServerInScope to assertMcpServerInCapabilityScope; :7952-7959 throws when isCapabilityAllowed(effective, serverId) is false. capability-scope-resolver.ts:31-58 computeEffectiveSet builds the set only from enabled assignment rows when not inheriting; :61-63 isCapabilityAllowed = set==='ALL' || set.has(ref). grep confirms goatcitadel-internal-* IDs are never inserted into capability scope assignments. The added test (capability-scope-mcp-enforcement.test.ts) covers fault/absent-resolver fail-closed but NOT the internal-server-in-scoped-workspace case, indicating the regression was unconsidered. Pre-fix code exempted internal servers: `if (!isInternalMcpApprovalInboxServer(server) && !isInternalMcpDurableTasksServer(server)) this.host.assertMcpServerInScope?.(input)`.
verifyEvidence: Reproduced against HEAD a81eeccc4. The real GatewayService.assertMcpServerInCapabilityScope gate (gateway-service.ts:7942), wired with a resolver whose listAllMcpServerIds includes the two internal IDs exactly as production does (readMcpServers()->buildGatewayOwnedInternalMcpServers ALWAYS prepends goatcitadel-internal-approval-inbox and goatcitadel-internal-durable-tasks; gateway-service.ts:8744, 9859-9863, and listAllMcpServerIds maps listMcpServers() at :1018), throws PolicyViolationError for BOTH internal server IDs the moment a citadel has any curated mcp_server grant that does not explicitly list them. computeEffectiveSet (capability-scope-resolver.ts:31-58) intersects to only the enabled grant refs; internal IDs are in allGlobal but never in the grant rows, so they are excluded -> isCapabilityAllowed=false. Baseline (unconfigured scope) correctly allows them. git show 29ebf44a8 confirms the fix removed the pre-fix internal-server exemption and now calls enforceMcpServerScope(input) UNCONDITIONALLY at tool-invocation-coordinator-service.ts:927 before the internal dispatch at :931/:938; invokeMcpTool->executeMcpRuntime (coordinator :795) is the sole path and has no upstream internal bypass. Second part also confirmed: same diff flips the resolver fault fallback from ALL_CAPABILITIES (fail-open) to NO_CAPABILITIES (capability-scope-resolver.ts:93), so a transient resolver fault now denies ALL MCP including internal. The added capability-scope-mcp-enforcement.test.ts uses listAllMcpServerIds=['allowed','denied'] and never covers the internal-server-in-scoped-workspace case, so the regression was unconsidered. Genuine governance/safety-path DoS in exactly the workspaces capability scoping targets. Repro tests passed 3/3 and were removed after.
repro: Static: in a workspace whose citadel or workspace has at least one enabled mcp_server capability assignment (curated MCP allowlist not including the two goatcitadel-internal IDs), invoke mcp.invoke with serverId=goatcitadel-internal-approval-inbox or goatcitadel-internal-durable-tasks. enforceMcpServerScope→assertMcpServerInCapabilityScope throws PolicyViolationError and the call returns ok:false reasonCodes:['mcp_capability_scope_denied']. Also: make listAssignmentsForScope throw and observe every internal MCP invocation is now denied (NO_CAPABILITIES).

title: Autonomy kill-switch fix silently loses queued autonomous durable runs (no resume after un-pause)
claim: The GW-concurrency-1 fix blocks autonomous durable runs by THROWING from the executor (durable-execution-service.ts:591 assertAutonomousDurableRunAllowed, and chat-proactive-service.ts:2165). A thrown executor error is not parked/retried on this path: the durable worker's drainQueuedRuns catch (durable-run-service.ts:981) routes it straight to failWorkflowRun (:1400), which sets the run to terminal 'failed' (onRunFailed at gateway-service.ts:1268 only records a signal — it does NOT schedule a retry). Neither drainQueuedRuns (scans 'queued') nor reconcileRecoverableRuns (scans expired-'running', :900/:905) re-drives 'failed' runs, and disengaging the kill switch (AutonomyControlService.setKillSwitch -> updateFeatureFlags, gateway-service.ts:1607) has no re-drive of failed autonomous runs. So a queued/in-flight proactive.tick, autonomous chat.turn, or autonomous connector-delivery run that is dequeued during a kill-switch window becomes 'failed' and STUCK — it does not resume when autonomy is re-enabled; recovery requires a manual retryDurableRun/recoverDeadLetter. The operator engages a safety PAUSE and gets a silent permanent CANCEL of already-queued autonomy, with only a durable_run_failed event as the signal. The resume guard added at durable-run-service.ts:500 does not help because the loss happens via the fail path, not the paused path.
evidence: durable-execution-service.ts:590-592 (proactive.tick execute throws via assertAutonomousDurableRunAllowed); :1063/:1189 same for connector delivery/chat turn; drainQueuedRuns catch at durable-run-service.ts:977-985 calls failWorkflowRun (not scheduleRunningWorkflowRetry); failWorkflowRun:1400-1443 marks 'failed' and calls onRunFailed which (gateway-service.ts:1268-1273) only records improvement signal; reconcileRecoverableRuns:900 only reclaims expired-running; no auto re-drive of 'failed' on flag flip (gateway-service.ts:1604-1616). No test asserts a kill-switch-blocked run is parked/resumable — the added tests (durable-execution-service.test.ts:708/1026) only assert the throw.
verifyEvidence: Regression confirmed by static trace against HEAD a81eeccc4. The GW-concurrency-1 fix added assertAutonomousDurableRunAllowed throws in the executors (durable-execution-service.ts:591 proactive.tick, :1063 connector delivery, :1189 chat.turn) plus a diff-confirmed resume guard at durable-run-service.ts:500 and a maybeEnqueueAutonomousDelivery guard at :1311. The throw path routes through drainQueuedRuns catch (durable-run-service.ts:977-985), which — because the kill-switch error is not a timeout — calls failWorkflowRun (:1400). failWorkflowRun calls persistFailedRun (:1409/:1472), setting status='failed' with finishedAt; isTerminalRunStatus (:1509-1511) includes 'failed', so it is terminal with NO retry ladder (no scheduleRunningWorkflowRetry, no dead-letter transition). onRunFailed (gateway-service.ts:1268-1273) only records an improvement signal. The added resume guard only covers paused->queued (resumeDurableRun rejects any non-'paused' status at :497-498), so it cannot help a 'failed' run. setKillSwitch (gateway-service.ts:1607 -> AutonomyControlService.setKillSwitch :139-140) only flips the flag with no re-drive. evaluateDurableContinuationGate (gateway-service.ts:4594-4610) checks only step-count metrics, NOT the kill switch, so it does not intercept the run as paused/cancelled before the throw. claimNextQueuedRun / isLeaseAcquisitionPaused (:950/:1307) are event-loop-lag backpressure only and do not gate on autonomyV1Disabled, so a run queued before the switch IS claimed and hits the throw. Added tests (durable-execution-service.test.ts:708/1026/1531) only assert rejects.toThrow(/autonomy kill switch/i) and that downstream dispatch is skipped — none assert a resumable/parked state. Net: a proactive.tick / autonomous chat.turn / autonomous connector-delivery run that is queued or in-flight when the kill switch is engaged becomes permanently 'failed' and is not resumed on flag flip; recovery needs a manual retryDurableRun. Genuine (if narrow-window) regression: the operator engages a temporary safety pause and silently, permanently cancels already-queued autonomy.
repro: Static + partial dynamic: (1) added tests only assert rejects.toThrow(/autonomy kill switch/i), never a resumable/paused state. (2) Trace: enqueue autonomous chat.turn -> engage autonomyV1Disabled -> worker claimNextQueuedRun -> executeWorkflow throws -> drainQueuedRuns catch -> failWorkflowRun -> status 'failed'. Disengage flag -> run stays 'failed'. Full e2e: mock DurableRunService.deps.workflowRegistry.executeWorkflow to throw the kill-switch error for a queued run, drive requestRunProcessing, assert getRun(runId).status==='failed' and that a later flag flip + requestRunProcessing does not change it to 'queued'/'completed'.

title: Windows MCP stdio spawn still throws EINVAL synchronously — every command:npx MCP server fails to launch on Windows (unfixed High)
claim: withStdioMcpClient spawns resolveSpawnCommand()'s `.cmd` rewrite with shell:false and no cmd.exe wrapper, so on modern Node (CVE-2024-27980 fix) spawn('npx.cmd', ...) throws EINVAL synchronously — bypassing the child.on('error') handler at :725 — for both MCP discovery (listMcpTools) and invocation (invokeMcpRuntimeTool). This is the original XC-windows-parity-1; the fix commits never touched this code path even though they applied the correct cmd.exe /d /s /c wrapper to sibling scripts.
evidence: mcp-runtime.ts:657 command=resolveSpawnCommand(server.command??''); :658-664 spawn(command, server.args??[], {stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe'],cwd,env,windowsHide:true,timeout}) — no shell, no cmd.exe. resolveSpawnCommand:1240-1242 returns `${command}.cmd` on win32. Contrast the correct pattern the same fix batch used at scripts/typescript/run-ts7-workspace.mjs:156-162 (spawn(ComSpec,['/d','/s','/c',windowsCommand])). git diff 67c3adb64..a81eeccc4 -- apps/gateway/src/services/mcp-runtime.ts shows no change to the spawn/resolveSpawnCommand region.
verifyEvidence: Confirmed unfixed by static analysis + Node version. withStdioMcpClient (mcp-runtime.ts:657) sets command=resolveSpawnCommand(server.command??'') and at :658-664 calls spawn(command, args, {stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe'],cwd,env,windowsHide:true,timeout}) — shell:false, no cmd.exe wrapper. resolveSpawnCommand (:1240-1242) returns `${command}.cmd` for npm/npx/pnpm/yarn on win32 (verified by test mcp-runtime.test.ts:365 asserting resolveSpawnCommand('npx','win32',...)==='npx.cmd'). The spawn call is NOT wrapped in try/catch and child.on('error') is only attached at :725, after the synchronous spawn. This environment runs Node v24.14.0, past the CVE-2024-27980 fix (>=18.20.2/20.12.2/21.7.3), under which spawning a .cmd/.bat with shell:false throws EINVAL synchronously on Windows — bypassing the error handler. The same fix batch applied the correct ComSpec /d /s /c wrapper to a sibling (scripts/typescript/run-ts7-workspace.mjs:156-162), but git diff 67c3adb64..a81eeccc4 -- mcp-runtime.ts shows the only change was refactoring sanitizeMcpRuntimeError to redactSecretText; the spawn/resolveSpawnCommand region is untouched. No ComSpec/windowsVerbatimArguments/shell present anywhere in mcp-runtime.ts. So every command:npx (etc.) stdio MCP server fails to launch on Windows for both listMcpTools discovery and invokeMcpRuntimeTool. Real Windows functional break; correctly flagged as pre-existing/unfixed.
repro: On Windows Node >=20.12/22: configure any stdio MCP server with command:'npx', args:['-y','@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem','.']; call listMcpTools or invokeMcpRuntimeTool -> spawn throws EINVAL before the error handler attaches, surfacing as an unhandled synchronous throw / hard failure. Static: read mcp-runtime.ts:657-664 + :1240-1242. Existing tests do NOT catch it (spawn mocked; test asserts the buggy .cmd string at mcp-runtime.test.ts:365).

title: Self-improvement cron fix makes an enabled config row silently no-op (worse than prior generic-task fallback)
claim: The XC-config-drift-4 fix assigns action=improvement to the config-seeded cron row self_improvement_weekly_replay, but the improvement scheduler still keys off a DIFFERENT row (improvement_weekly). An operator who enables the config row now triggers the improvement dispatch which immediately returns because the OTHER row is disabled — a silent no-op. Two duplicate rows with identical display name still seed at startup.
evidence: cron-job-config-helpers.ts:30 BUILT_IN_CRON_ACTIONS maps self_improvement_weekly_replay -> improvement, and cron-job-config-helpers.ts:133 forces that action on load. cron-automation-service.ts:29 IMPROVEMENT_WEEKLY_JOB_ID=self_improvement_weekly_replay, but improvement-service.ts:476/510/514 hardcode improvement_weekly and never import the constant (confirmed by grep). Startup gateway-service.ts:2157-2158 seeds BOTH rows. Dispatch cron-automation-service.ts:380 (action===improvement) -> runHandlers.improvement() (gateway-service.ts:1221) -> runWeeklyImprovementSchedulerIfDue() -> cronJobs.get('improvement_weekly') then `if (!job?.enabled) return` (improvement-service.ts:476-479) BEFORE the force check. loop43.test.ts:75-76 comment confirms the scheduler skips disabled jobs even under force. Pre-fix (67c3adb64) the config row had no action -> defaulted to task -> enabling it created an inbox task; the fix changed the failure mode to a silent no-op.
verifyEvidence: Reproduced against HEAD a81eeccc4. Two distinct cron rows with the same display name 'Self-Improvement Weekly Replay': (a) the config-seeded row jobId=self_improvement_weekly_replay, forced action=improvement by BUILT_IN_CRON_ACTIONS (cron-job-config-helpers.ts:29-35 maps IMPROVEMENT_WEEKLY_JOB_ID->improvement; :120,133 forces it on load; IMPROVEMENT_WEEKLY_JOB_ID='self_improvement_weekly_replay' per cron-automation-service.ts:29; config/cron-jobs.example.json:4-9 now carries action:improvement,enabled:false), and (b) the scheduler-owned row jobId='improvement_weekly' seeded by ensureWeeklyImprovementCronJob (improvement-service.ts:514) at startup (gateway-service.ts:2158). Dispatch action===improvement (cron-automation-service.ts:380) -> runHandlers.improvement (gateway-service.ts:1220) -> runWeeklyImprovementSchedulerIfDue({force:true}) which reads cronJobs.get('improvement_weekly') and returns early if !job?.enabled (improvement-service.ts:476-479) BEFORE any force handling. My repro seeded improvement_weekly (disabled), enabled ONLY self_improvement_weekly_replay, force-ran the scheduler, and asserted listDecisionReplayRuns(5)===[] — passed: a silent no-op. Regression confirmed: git show 67c3adb64 has NO action on the config example row and no BUILT_IN_CRON_ACTIONS map, so pre-fix enabling it defaulted to action='task' (inbox task); the fix changed the failure mode to a silent no-op. Repro tests passed 2/2 and were removed after.
repro: vitest: create Storage, write config/cron-jobs.json with {jobId:self_improvement_weekly_replay, action:improvement, enabled:false}, call loadCronJobsFromConfig(host) then service.ensureWeeklyImprovementCronJob(); enable ONLY the config row via cronJobs.upsert({...,enabled:true}); await service.runWeeklyImprovementSchedulerIfDue({force:true}); assert service.listDecisionReplayRuns(5)===[]. Fix: point improvement-service at IMPROVEMENT_WEEKLY_JOB_ID so config, action map, and scheduler share one jobId, and stop ensureWeeklyImprovementCronJob from seeding a second row.

title: run-unless-env.mjs pnpm.cmd spawn is synchronous-EINVAL-fatal on Windows (unfixed) — breaks default gateway test/smoke prebuild
claim: The gateway pretest/presmoke hook spawns pnpm.cmd with shell:false and no try/catch; the synchronous EINVAL on modern Node escapes child.on('error') at :23, crashing `pnpm --filter @goatcitadel/gateway test`/smoke at the extensions-sdk prebuild on Windows. XC-supply-chain-2 remains unfixed (file untouched); its claimed duplicate root XC-windows-parity-1 was also not fixed.
evidence: scripts/run-unless-env.mjs:16-21 spawn(resolveCommand(command), args, {cwd,env,stdio:'inherit',shell:false}); resolveCommand:39-44 returns 'pnpm.cmd' on win32. No wrapping try/catch. File absent from git diff --stat 67c3adb64..a81eeccc4.
verifyEvidence: Reproduced directly on this Windows host (Node v24.14.0). Running the exact gateway pretest/presmoke command `node scripts/run-unless-env.mjs GOATCITADEL_SKIP_EXTENSIONS_SDK_PREBUILD pnpm --filter @goatcitadel/extensions-sdk build` (apps/gateway/package.json:48,54) crashes with an UNCAUGHT `Error: spawn EINVAL` originating at run-unless-env.mjs:16:15 and exits code 1. Cause confirmed empirically: on patched modern Node, spawn('pnpm.cmd', args, {shell:false}) throws EINVAL SYNCHRONOUSLY; the child.on('error') handler is registered at :23 AFTER the throwing spawn at :16 and there is no try/catch, so the async handler never fires (verified asyncErrorFired:false). resolveCommand (:39-44) returns 'pnpm.cmd' on win32. Escape hatch GOATCITADEL_SKIP_EXTENSIONS_SDK_PREBUILD=1 exits cleanly (0) via the early return at :11-14. File confirmed ABSENT from git diff 67c3adb64..a81eeccc4 (unfixed). Correctly labeled a pre-existing (non-fix-range) Windows-parity break; only affects the default local gateway test/smoke prebuild on Windows (CI is Linux) and has a working documented bypass.
repro: On Windows: `pnpm --filter @goatcitadel/gateway test` (invokes pretest -> node scripts/run-unless-env.mjs GOATCITADEL_SKIP_EXTENSIONS_SDK_PREBUILD pnpm --filter ... build) -> spawn throws EINVAL synchronously -> uncaught. Escape hatch GOATCITADEL_SKIP_EXTENSIONS_SDK_PREBUILD=1 still works. Static: read scripts/run-unless-env.mjs:16-44.

title: verify-extension-package-artifacts.mjs tar extract lacks --force-local — publish gate fails on Windows GNU/MSYS2 tar (unfixed)
claim: spawnSync('tar', ['-xzf', <absolute C:\ tmp tarball>, '-C', extractDir]) has no --force-local, so GNU/MSYS2 tar (common on Windows dev PATHs before bsdtar) interprets the C: drive letter as an rsh host and fails, breaking verify:extensions:package and the fast.extensions-sdk-package lane. XC-supply-chain-3 remains unfixed (file untouched).
evidence: scripts/verify-extension-package-artifacts.mjs:64 spawnSync('tar',['-xzf',tarball,'-C',extractDir],{encoding,shell:false}); tarball derived from os.tmpdir() (:48 mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(),...))). File absent from git diff --stat 67c3adb64..a81eeccc4. resolvePnpmPackArgs special-cases Windows for pnpm pack but the tar calls were not given --force-local.
verifyEvidence: Underlying tar bug reproduced with GNU tar 1.35 (Git Bash /usr/bin/tar) using the script's exact shape: created a tarball under a C:\ tmp dir and ran `tar -xzf C:\...\archive.tgz -C C:\...\extract` -> 'tar (child): Cannot connect to C: resolve failed', exit 2 — matching the finding's predicted error. scripts/verify-extension-package-artifacts.mjs:64 spawnSync('tar',['-xzf',tarball,'-C',extractDir],{encoding,shell:false}) has no --force-local; tarball derives from os.tmpdir() (:48). The file is absent from git diff --stat 67c3adb64..a81eeccc4 (unchanged); resolvePnpmPackArgs (:289-294) special-cases Windows for pnpm pack but the tar calls (:64, :230) were not given --force-local. grep confirms no --force-local anywhere in scripts/. TWO CAVEATS that bound impact to Medium: (1) The finding's CI claim is FALSE — both lanes running verify:extensions:package are ubuntu-latest (publish-extensions-sdk.yml:15 and verification-1-0-release-proof.yml runner: ubuntu-latest), so no Windows CI lane hits this; the 'fast.extensions-sdk-package lane' break is overstated. (2) Default Windows (PowerShell/cmd) resolves tar to C:\Windows\system32\tar.exe = bsdtar 3.8.4, which handles C:\ paths fine; only GNU-tar-first-on-PATH dev shells (Git Bash/MSYS2/Cygwin) fail. Real but narrow Windows-dev-only issue; correctly flagged unfixed. Severity Medium confirmed.
repro: In Git Bash w/ GNU tar 1.35 on Windows: run node scripts/verify-extension-package-artifacts.mjs -> `tar -xzf C:\...\goatcitadel-ext-pack-XXX\...tgz` -> 'tar: Cannot connect to C: resolve failed', exit 2. Static: read scripts/verify-extension-package-artifacts.mjs:48,64.

title: Flaky useChatOutboundExecution stream/reconciliation tests (pre-existing, not a fix regression)
claim: The useChatOutboundExecution suite fails non-deterministically at varying assertions (observed failing lines 1618, 1753, 1995, 2073 across runs; then 29/29 green on 3 consecutive isolated re-runs). The flakiness is a fake-timer + microtask race against a module-level `let latest` harness (line 68), not a regression from the fix range: the only source change in range (useChatOutboundExecution.ts:951 `queuedOutbound.length > 0`) is unrelated to the flaking abort/reconciliation assertions, and the only test change in range was a new passing assertion (test.tsx:870).
evidence: Ran `vitest run src/chat/useChatOutboundExecution.test.tsx`: failure line differed each run (2073 during full-dir run, 1618+1753 next, 1995 next), then 3 consecutive isolated runs all passed 29/29. Failing tests use vi.useFakeTimers()+vi.advanceTimersByTime(400)+await Promise.resolve() (lines 1716,1748-1751) with shared module-level `latest` (line 68); failures cluster after heavy prior runs (267s import) indicating load/scheduling sensitivity.
verifyEvidence: Diff analysis verified exactly against the 67c3adb64..a81eeccc4 range: the ONLY source change to useChatOutboundExecution.ts is line 951 `queuedOutbound.some((item) => !item.paused)` -> `queuedOutbound.length > 0` (a paused-queued status tweak), and the ONLY test change is a new PASSING assertion at test.tsx:870 ('reports queued status even when all queued outbound items are paused') — both unrelated to the flaking abort/reconciliation assertions. The module-level `let latest` harness (test.tsx:68) and the vi.useFakeTimers()+vi.advanceTimersByTime(0/400)+await Promise.resolve() reconciliation flush (test.tsx:1716,1743-1751, with a telltale conditional `if (loadSessionCoreState.mock.calls.length === 0)` guard) are present and are a credible microtask/fake-timer non-determinism source. Isolated run passed 29/29. I could NOT reproduce a failure in 6 runs (1 isolated + 4 full src/chat at 261/261 + repeats), so the intermittent failure itself is unconfirmed, but the mechanism is real. Finding correctly self-declares this as pre-existing flakiness, NOT a fix regression, and not a code defect — a test-hygiene note only.
repro: cd packages/threaded-surface-core && npx vitest run src/chat  (fails intermittently in useChatOutboundExecution.test.tsx at differing lines); re-run the file in isolation and it goes green — confirms non-determinism, not a code defect from the fix.

title: Windows shell-arg hardening rejects '%' and drops backslash-escaping — edge-case crash for args with percent or trailing backslash
claim: The fix batch replaced Windows arg-escaping with assertSafeWindowsCommandArg that THROWS if a value contains '"', '%', CR/LF or NUL, and changed quoting from escaped to bare `"${value}"`. For the controlled inputs that flow through these helpers today (pnpm/package names, build paths) this is safe, but any future arg containing a literal '%' (legitimate on Windows) or a path ending in a backslash would now either throw or produce a mis-parsed `"...\"` at the CommandLineToArgvW layer.
evidence: scripts/dev.mjs:157-174 quoteWindowsCommandArg calls assertSafeWindowsCommandArg (:168-174 throws on /["%\r\n\0]/) and returns `"${value}"` with no backslash escaping (old code did value.replace(/(["\\])/g,'\\$1')). Identical pattern in run-ts7-workspace.mjs:172-189, build-bundle.mjs, build-desktop.mjs, bin/goatcitadel.mjs (per git show 2eefaa041). Callers today pass only package names (dev.mjs:143 ['--filter',pkg,...]).
verifyEvidence: Static + local repro against HEAD a81eeccc4. git show 2eefaa041 confirms the fix replaced the backslash-escaping return with assertSafeWindowsCommandArg(value) that THROWS on /["%\r\n\0]/ (dev.mjs:168-174) plus bare quoting `"${value}"` (dev.mjs:165) with NO backslash-escaping; identical pattern verified in run-ts7-workspace.mjs, packaging/build-bundle.mjs:574-585, packaging/build-desktop.mjs:155-166, bin/goatcitadel.mjs:1956-1967. Reproduced both edges by replicating the exact functions: an arg containing '%' throws the hardening error, and a spaced path ending in a backslash produces a trailing `\"` that mis-parses at CommandLineToArgvW.
